briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 4, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Global Disaster Warnings and the Reality of Compound Disasters
sections.content: The United Nations has declared that the 1.5-degree climate change defense line has effectively collapsed, warning that global warming is spiraling towards a catastrophic situation [7, 80, 88, 95, 100]. This warning is manifesting in the devastating reality of large-scale floods and landslides in Nepal, where over 1,200 people have died, and the search for missing persons from a hydroelectric power plant continues [3, 10, 13, 63, 68, 69, 82, 85]. Furthermore, the pattern of 'compound disasters' is becoming clear, with droughts and record-breaking heavy rainfall occurring consecutively after a 42.5°C heatwave [11]. The risk of major floods is also increasing as Himalayan glaciers melt faster due to soot [65].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Impacts and the Need for Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, the impacts of climate change are also becoming visible. As parks, such as Baebongsan Park in Seoul, change their appearance with mushrooms growing on park decks, Seoul City Council members emphasized the urgent need to establish and transition to park and forest safety management systems adapted to climate change [4, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17]. In the seas off Jeju, sea cucumber catches plummeted from 100kg to just 10 pieces, demonstrating the severe impact of the climate crisis on local livelihoods [66]. Meanwhile, the East Asian Seas Environmental Management Partnership (EAS EMP) Forum was held in Busan, where discussions on environmental issues, including climate change, took place [1, 5].

sections.title: 🌱 Trends in Carbon Neutrality Implementation and Accelerated Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Efforts to implement carbon neutrality are continuing across the country. Yesan County took its first step towards carbon-neutral finance by preparing the first greenhouse gas reduction-aware budget statement in Chungnam Province [18, 28, 37]. Several local governments, including Taebaek City and Yangpyeong County, are also participating in strengthening carbon neutrality implementation and practices [20, 25, 38]. Hyundai Motor Group signed an MOU for eco-friendly mobility with Oman, accelerating its transition to carbon neutrality through the operation of hydrogen electric buses and the establishment of EV charging infrastructure [21, 24, 26, 29, 36, 39]. The Korea Green Foundation and Evezary supported the carbon-neutral hosting of the Seoul International Environmental Film Festival by donating carbon credits [30, 32, 40]. In the renewable energy sector, the government significantly expanded the scope of renewable energy generators subject to remote output control installation to enhance grid stability [44, 45]. Local governments such as Gunsan City and Gyeongnam Province are promoting the dissemination of renewable energy by supporting household solar panel installations and expanding solar power in senior community centers [51, 53, 56, 62].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Response and Challenges
sections.content: Internationally, the Australian Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) has forecast the strongest El Niño on record, warning that preparations must be made for the largest El Niño in 1,000 years [70, 71, 102, 103]. This is expected to exacerbate extreme weather phenomena worldwide. Meanwhile, challenges persist in the international community's efforts to respond to climate change. The Texas A&M System decided to exclude climate change courses from its core curriculum, raising concerns about the shrinking scope of climate education in academia [72, 93, 98]. Concurrently, Amnesty International urged the protection of Angolan women and children displaced by drought and climate change, emphasizing that the climate crisis is deepening into a humanitarian issue [79].

briefing.closing: The news briefed today highlights the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the diverse domestic and international efforts simultaneously underway to overcome it. Responding to climate change is no longer an option but a necessity, and our collective sustained interest and action are becoming increasingly crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing for September 4, 2026.
